about: The Tour (shell/tour.js): each slide plays a title card, then its steps on the before tree, then on the after tree (once per option). Steps are the harness's step runner (runtime/steps.ts) plus the paced ones in runtime/tour.ts: hover (draws the element's tooltip), highlight (after only unless both), scroll, typeSlow, selectLine, hold. open: the scenario's own open steps, played paced (default), fast, or skip. beforeSide / afterSide override scenario, steps or open per side; options replace the after pass; surface phone plays pages (one scenario each).

slides.title: Settings in six sections
slides.caption: One short page — Models, Keys, Voice, Box, Safety, Appearance — instead of a long scroll of every knob. Key sync, mission host, schedules and sync intervals leave the UI.

slides.title: Models: one picker per role
slides.caption: Chat, Background and Voice each get one picker from the live OpenRouter list. There is no Images & PDFs row: images and PDFs go to the Chat model, and only if it can't read them to a built-in vision model.

slides.title: Pick a model, it's checked for its role
slides.caption: No capability table: each picker opens the chat's search-and-scroll menu, and the model you pick is checked for what its role needs (Chat: tools and images; Background: tools; Voice: images and PDFs). One line says Passed, or what's missing.

slides.title: Keys, trimmed
slides.caption: OpenRouter first, then the service keys you actually use; the other providers fold away with a count of how many are set.

slides.title: The Box section
slides.caption: Everything about the box in one place: where it is and whether this vault syncs to it. Sync intervals and the key-sync blurb are gone.

slides.title: The context dial counts cached tokens once
slides.caption: On a long cached chat the dial used to add the cached tokens on top of the prompt and read about twice the real size. Now it shows the real number against the model's real window.

slides.title: The dial is there when you reopen a chat
slides.caption: Before, the dial only appeared after you sent something. Now a reopened chat shows the context its last turn reported.

slides.title: Near the limit of a 1M-window model
slides.caption: At 880k the dial is red against Sonnet 5.5's real 1M window, and the tooltip says the next message first summarizes the earlier conversation. Before, it was pegged against a fixed 200k.

slides.title: A small-window model
slides.caption: Qwen3 32B has a 131k window: at 120k the dial is red and the next message compacts first, so the prompt fits. Before, it looked amber against an assumed 200k and the next prompt would be rejected.

slides.title: Notes search finds what a row shows
slides.caption: “failure modes” is in a note's title. Now the search matches the title, highlighted text and summary, in any word order, and the count leaves out cleared notes.

slides.title: @-mentions rank names that start with what you typed
slides.caption: A long file name that starts with “eigengap” used to sink below short names that merely contain it. Now: name starts with, then name contains, then path.

slides.title: History reads like a timeline
slides.caption: Ctrl+H used to list raw commits — autosaves, app-state churn, hashes. Now it groups saves into sessions, hides the app's own files, and shows agent turns, the box, missions, restores and undos as plain entries.

slides.title: Undo one agent turn
slides.caption: Pick what the agent did and undo just that change, as one new commit. The entry is struck through and offers Redo.

slides.title: Redo an undone change
slides.caption: An undone edit stays in the timeline, struck through. Redo brings it back, again as one commit.

slides.title: Restore a version of a note
slides.caption: A note's versions are one per session, not one per save. Preview or diff one against now, then restore it; the open note reloads with that text.

slides.title: Three ways to show history — pick one
slides.caption: The same timeline in three places: A a modal like today's, B a side sheet next to the note, C a thin version strip above the note.

slides.title: Restoring, in each style
slides.caption: The same restore — an older version of the scaling-laws note — done from the modal, the sheet, and the inline strip.

slides.title: Mission Control is gone
slides.caption: The Rocket opened Mission Control (missions, schedules, notifications). Missions are gone, and so is the bell: notifications live on the phone.

slides.title: Approve & run is gone
slides.caption: A chat where the agent once proposed a mission: the Approve & run card is now a plain plan block — there is no missions system to start.

slides.title: The Schedules panel is gone
slides.caption: Recurring schedules leave the app: Ctrl+Shift+S no longer opens a Schedules panel, and the agent has no Schedule tool. The engine's one-off wake (keep-going mode) stays.

slides.title: The North star prompt editor is gone
slides.caption: The compass opened an editor for the agent's prompt files, including the supervisor's. With missions gone it goes too; supervisor.md is no longer created.

slides.title: Chats grouped by project — pick a layout
slides.caption: Each project is a section of the chat list, chats without a project keep Running / Recent / Earlier, and the old mission threads fold into Archived missions.

slides.title: A project chip on every chat — pick where it sits
slides.caption: Set a chat's project from the chat itself: type a project's name (or a new one) and the chat moves into that section.

options.label: Option B — beside the model picker

slides.title: New chat in a project
slides.caption: From a project's chip, start a fresh chat that is already in that project.

slides.title: The ongoing-work line
slides.caption: Over the composer, one line says what a chat's long work is doing: working, waiting on its next check, waiting for you, or blocked — with what it has cost.

slides.title: Phone: Activity and the feedback screen are gone
slides.caption: The menu has no Activity (missions, workers, schedules), Approve & run is gone, and the drawer is just Box & settings.

slides.title: Phone: projects, the archive, ongoing work, notifications
slides.caption: Conversations grouped by project with Archived missions folded at the bottom, a project sheet on the chat title, the ongoing-work line, and notification cards that open their conversation.

pages.label: A chat with its project and ongoing work

slides.title: The phone page, rebuilt in React — identical
slides.caption: The phone app is now a bundled React + TypeScript app instead of one big HTML file with in-browser Babel. It looks exactly like today's page with all the changes above: watch the same pages in both.

slides.title: Chat runs on the box — and says so when it can't
slides.caption: With a box configured, every chat turn runs on the box. When the box can't be reached, the composer is disabled and says why, instead of quietly running the agent on the laptop.

steps.label: Box unreachable — agent runs on the box

slides.title: Subagents: one task, split across two helpers
slides.caption: On the box, the agent can hand pieces of work to subagents that run in parallel. Known Phase 3 issue, shown as it renders today: one delegation shows three tool entries (the call, plus a duplicate “Subagent” record per child), and each child's state and cost are stored but not shown.

slides.title: Done is checked by a separate verifier
slides.caption: When the agent says it's done, a second model checks the evidence and its verdict is the last line of the Done step; the agent repeats it to you. Three verdicts, as they render — only that line (and a notification) shows them.

slides.title: Keep-going: a wake arrives, works, and sleeps again
slides.caption: A chat in keep-going mode schedules its own next check (“next 3:40” over the composer). When the wake fires, “⏰ Wake: …” appears, the turn works and reports, and the line moves to the next check. Before: the laptop has no wakes, so nothing arrives.

slides.title: Roll-over: a long chat moves to a fresh session
slides.caption: When a box chat outgrows the model's window, the engine continues in a fresh session with a recap. The transcript shows one quiet line; the recap is stored on it but there's no way to read it on the desktop yet.

steps.text: Rolled over to a fresh session
steps.label: roll-over

slides.title: An image from the laptop, in box mode
slides.caption: Paste a chart and ask about it. Today the laptop runs the turn and reads the image. In box mode the message is NOT sent — “Images can't be sent to the box yet”. That's how this tree behaves; sending images to the box isn't built.

slides.title: A chat from a few seconds ago says “now”
slides.caption: The chat list printed a clock for anything under a minute old (“0:04”, “0:08”). Now it says “now”. Watch the time on the “Quick question about muP” row.

slides.title: That's everything — and what's yours to decide

sections.title: In this tour
items: Settings: six sections, roles (no Images & PDFs row), capabilities, keys, Box
Chat details: the context dial, compaction divider, Ctrl+K/L models, the PDF tool, search
History: the timeline, undo, redo, restore, three styles
Removals: Mission Control, Approve & run, schedules, the North star editor; chats by project, the project chip, the ongoing-work line, notifications
Phone: the same changes, rebuilt in React
Phase 2: chat on the box — unreachable box, subagents, the Done verifier, wakes, roll-over, images, “now”

sections.title: Your decisions
items: Capability view: A table · B one line per picker · C folded
Ctrl+K / Ctrl+L roles: A both Chat · B K Background, L Chat (default) · C both Background
History: A modal · B side sheet · C inline strip
Chat list: A projects as sections · B projects as folders
Project chip: A over the thread · B beside the model picker
Notifications: A popover · B side panel
Built-in vision model for images the Chat model can't read: Gemini 3.5 Flash (no setting)
Serve the React phone app at /phone (built, off until you approve)
Duplicate subagent records: fold each child's “Subagent” record into the one subagent call (with its state and cost), or drop the records?
Images from the laptop in box mode are refused today: send them to the box, or keep the refusal for now?
Roll-over recap and the verifier's notes are stored but barely shown: open the recap from the roll-over line, like the compaction divider?
